note:
# P-E-2019-1903455-a52f7980 - 2019 ICM E, team 1903455

## What the paper is
An ecosystem-service index built from eleven indicators (EWM for weights, CVM for values),
hierarchical clustering to sort four land-use projects by intensity, a bio-cost valuation
model fitted with a logistic curve, and an SVM forecast of the benefit-cost ratio to 2035.
Twenty numbered exhibits, thirteen figures and seven tables, over twenty-five pages.

## How it schedules its exhibits
Section 4 spends three figures and one table on defining the index (framework, wheel, gauge,
weights); Section 5 spends three figures and one table on making the model (combo chart,
logistic fit, two panel pairs); Section 6 spends one figure and one table on the result, one
figure on the sustainability effect, and one figure plus a table on the fitting; Section 7
spends the last two figures on the sensitivity sweep; the appendix repeats Table 4 three times.
The pattern is: one schematic per idea being DEFINED, one plot per number being PRODUCED, and
one table only where the numbers must be read in a grid that prose cannot carry.

## When it draws in three dimensions
Once, and only for a share-of-total breakdown: four exploded 3-D pies, one per project. No
other exhibit extrudes anything - all the curves are flat and all the schematics are flat.
The rule this paper hands you: if the quantity is a partition of 100%, a pie is acceptable
and the third dimension is decoration; if the quantity is a trend, use a line and never a 3-D
ribbon.

## Table shape against data size
Four columns and four rows (Table 3) is a roster - words only, booktabs. Two columns and four
rows (Table 5) is a list of fitted equations - booktabs. Five columns and sixteen rows with
merged group cells (Table 2) is a hierarchy of weights - fully boxed, colour fills, decimal
aligned. Nine columns and five rows with arrow glyphs (Table 4 and its three appendix copies)
is a curve encoded as cells - fully boxed, merged stub. The rule: the more the grid's cells
have to be compared positionally, the more rules it gets; a table read as a list gets
booktabs and nothing else.

## Caption templates
Two shapes, and the choice is positional, not stylistic:
- above the grid, no colon, no full stop: "Table N <noun phrase naming the object>"
  ("Table 2 Weight values of the indicators", "Table 5 Result of fitting according to
  Figure.11")
- below the plot, full stop after the number, no colon: "Figure.N <noun phrase naming the
  quantity, the units and the series> <full stop>" ("Figure.11 Benefit-cost ratio curve of
  four projects which influenced by sustainable development measures only")
Captions never state a result, never give units, never name a symbol. The two schematics get
four-word captions because the drawing is self-describing.

## Context-linking templates
- Definition exhibits open the paragraph that defines them: "The whole modeling process can
  be shown as follows: <figure>".
- Result exhibits are pointed at from the end of the sentence that explains the method:
  "... we make the cost of project PA and the discrete points of ESI and fit it with Gaussian
  method, such as Figure.5 shows. <figure> From the above Figure.5, we can see that ..."
- The read-back is always one sentence and always restates the trend, never the numbers:
  "As can be seen from Figure.6, the benefit-cost ratio of the four projects will increase
  first and then ..."
- Sensitivity exhibits are announced by parameter: "we calculate their real benefit-cost
  ratio, as shown in Figure 12", then read back as a monotone statement about the parameter
  ("with the increase of theta, the benefit-cost radio of the same project grows increasingly
  slowly").

## What this paper hands the lane
- A second furniture case: 25 identical stamps, so 'duplicate' must be the reason for
  page furniture whenever the geometry repeats exactly, and 'background' reserved for
  folio-like marks that vary.
- The omission twin of a known break: captions that exist in the layer but are CORRUPTED
  (watermark private-use glyphs spliced into Figure 8's caption; the theta symbol dropped
  from Figure 13's caption and from three body sentences), which needs a quote-as-prefix rule.
- The first printed-but-unboxed exhibit: Table 1 Notations is live text with no measured
  region, so the census's region count and its exhibit count differ by one and the difference
  has to be declared, not hidden.
- A template grid: Table 4 printed four times with only the stub moving, which is how this
  paper multiplies its appendix without a second design.

## The layer's own defects
Running head is live text with the folio inside it ("Team#1903455  Page 7 of 21"), so every
page's first line is furniture; the advert stamp contributes private-use glyphs that splice
into captions and equation runs; fullwidth commas appear inside a citation ("Appendix 1，2，3");
and Table 1 exists only as prose.
rules: Forty-seven measured regions on twenty-five pages, and they close with nothing left over: twenty printed exhibits (thirteen figures, seven tables) and twenty-seven exclusions - twenty-five of them the same box [place.section_path].

The furniture is the mirror image of the previous paper's: where that one boxed a thin rules band on two folio pages, this paper stamps THE SAME VECTOR BOX ON EVERY ONE OF ITS TWENTY-FIVE PAGES - pt y=767-839, 678 paths, area 0.020, aspect 2.0, holding the same four strings ('关注数学模型', '2', 'MATHmodels', '获取更多资讯'). Identical geometry, identical content, zero page dependence: filed as duplicates, never as background [place.page_zone].

Family mix of the thirteen figures: line 6 (Figures 5, 7, 8, 11, 12, 13), flowchart-or-schematic 3 (Figures 1, 2, 10), bar 2 (Figures 3, 4), scatter 1 (Figure 6) and other 1 (Figure 9's pies) [geometry.family].

Exactly one three-dimensional drawing in the paper and it is the ONLY exhibit whose marks have to be mentally un-distorted: Figure 9's four exploded 3-D pies, each disc drawn as a perspective ellipse with a side wall and one slice pulled out. Three of the four slices are 29/71, 33/67, 9/91, 46/54 - the extrusion adds nothing an arc would not carry [geometry.three_d].

Those pies are the reason the family vocabulary has an escape hatch: there is no pie family in the closed fourteen, and forcing them into bar would misdescribe both the marks (arcs) and the geometry (perspective). Filed other, with the note carrying the reason [geometry.family].

Legend placement tracks the NUMBER OF FRAMES, not the number of series: the seven exhibits that carry a key put it INSIDE, the one whose categories cannot fit the frame puts it outside-right (Figure 3), the four-panel row puts one shared key ABOVE the whole row (Figure 9), and the four exhibits with no key at all are the three schematics plus the two-panel dot scatter [geometry.legend].

Caption side divides by exhibit class and admits exactly one exception: all seven tables carry their caption ABOVE the grid, twelve of the thirteen figures carry it BELOW the artwork, and the exception is Figure 10, the icon montage on page 18, whose caption is printed above the drawing - the only exhibit in the paper whose caption precedes its own art (caption top at 275.3 pt against a region starting at 299.0) [caption.position].

Both caption numberings are printed WITHOUT a colon: figures as 'Figure.1' with a full stop and no space, tables as 'Table 2' with nothing after the number. The appendix is the only place a colon appears, in 'Appendix 1: ESVM result of project PB' - and those headings carry no table number at all [caption.numbering].

Caption length is bimodal by function, not by content: the two schematics take four words each ('Framework of ESVM', 'Ecological Services System.'), the sixteen remaining exhibits cluster between seven and sixteen words, and the two outliers are the two panel pairs, where the caption names every series it plots - 42 words for Figure 6, 68 for Figure 7 [caption.words].

Not one caption in the paper states a unit, names a variable, gives a condition or draws a conclusion, and not one is a sentence: all twenty are noun phrases with no finite verb, so the voice field is empty of evidence rather than passive [caption.voice].

Every caption is in the text layer, including the two damaged ones - so the paper's defects are not missing text but corrupted text, and the pass can quote a clean prefix where a full sentence does not survive [caption.verbatim].

Eighteen of the twenty exhibits are named by number and two are never named at all: the framework diagram, introduced only as 'The whole modeling process can be shown as follows:', and the ESS wheel, introduced by nothing [mention.first_page].

Two pointer grammars divide the paper almost evenly: thirteen 'direct' pointers that name the exhibit at the head of the sentence and five 'as-shown-in' pointers that bury it mid-clause ('As shown in Figure.4, ...', 'From the above Table 3 ...') [mention.lead_pattern].

One exhibit is named AFTER the page it is printed on: Table 3 sits on page 10 and its first pointer is on page 11 ('From the above Table 3 we can see'), the paper's only negative lead [mention.lead_pages].

Read-backs are short and mechanical: eight of the eighteen named exhibits are followed on the same page by exactly one sentence that restates the exhibit's own reading, and both Section 6 curve figures open their read-back with 'As can be seen from the Figure ...' [mention.read_sentences].

The six forecast plots share ONE repeated device, and it is the paper's entire visual grammar for prediction: a dashed vertical rule at 2019 with the words 'Forecast area' printed to its right, the observed half drawn solid and the predicted half dashed (Figures 5, 7, 8, 11, 12, 13) [geometry.family].

Figures 11, 12 and 13 are one drawing recipe rendered three times, and the difference between a result and a sensitivity check is carried ENTIRELY by the legend: Figure 11 keys the four curves by name ('Project A' to 'Project D'), Figure 12 keys them by fitted parameter value ('theta(Project A)=87.31'), Figure 13 drops the projects and keys the parameter levels ('theta=80' to 'theta=20') [geometry.legend].

Table 2 is the paper's weight grid and its most structured object: five columns, sixteen rows, a group weight VERTICALLY MERGED across each set of three children, a top-level 'Intensity' cell merged down the whole stub, and column fills (pink stub, lavender sub-weights, yellow final weights) doing the work a second header row would otherwise do [table.merged_cells].

Rule style is bimodal and it tracks the grid's job: the five grids whose cells must be read cell-by-cell are fully boxed (Table 2, Table 4 and the three appendices), while the two grids that are read as lists are booktabs with no verticals (Table 3, Table 5). No zebra anywhere, no diagonal header, no continued table - every table fits one page [table.rule_style].

Table 4 is the paper's answer to 'the figure drawn as a table': nine columns, a stub merged down four body rows, a binary N/Y column, a BCR/Description pair, and six year columns whose crossings are encoded as arrow glyphs plus the words 'Highest', 'Intersection', 'Zero' - the curve of Figure 8 written out cell by cell [table.merged_cells].

That same nine-column grid is printed FOUR times - once as Table 4 and again, unchanged in structure, as Appendix 1, 2 and 3 for projects PB, PC and PD, with only the stub and the six year columns moving. The paper's heaviest table is a template, and the appendices are its instantiations [place.section_kind].

Table 5 is the only grid whose cells are TYPESET MATHEMATICS rather than data: four fitted exponentials, which the prose then generalises into equation (22). Data flows table to model, not model to table [place.section_kind].

Two exhibits are measured as two boxes each - Figure 6's (a)/(b) pair on page 13 and Figure 7's (a)/(b) pair on page 16 - and the pass counts each pair ONCE, filing the right box as a fragment of the left one. On page 16 that gives the page three exhibits in one column of art (Figure 7 top, Figure 8 bottom) and the paper its only three-exhibit page [place.page_order].

Size is uncorrelated with rank in the argument: the largest exhibit is the framework diagram at 0.194 and the second largest the weight table at 0.186, but the four forecast panels that carry the paper's actual conclusions are among the smallest - Figure 8 at 0.157, Figure 11 at 0.125, Figure 12 at 0.073, Figure 13 at 0.070 [place.area_frac].

Section kinds are spread by chapter rather than by exhibit type: introduction holds the framework, model holds the SVM panels, result holds the four forecast plots and the grids they produce, and both sensitivity figures sit alone in Section 7 [place.section_kind].
Placement within the page is unremarkable and the paper never gives an exhibit a page to itself: ten mids, six tops, four bottoms and no solo page across twenty exhibits [place.page_zone].

The paper's own notation table is PRINTED BUT NEVER BOXED: 'Table 1 Notations' occupies live text at the top of page 4 and the layout pass produced no region for it, so the census has twenty numbered tables' worth of claims - errors, assumptions and notations - in the prose and only seven table rows. This is the lane's first exhibit that exists in the text layer and nowhere in the measurement layer [caption.verbatim].

The pass found the exhibits from their own furniture, not from their captions: the paper's advert stamp repeats 678 vector paths on every page, which makes any page with 159 or 233 paths a real drawing - Table 4 and the appendices (159 paths each), Table 2 (233), the project roster (3 paths plus typed cells), the fitting table (3 paths plus its equation images) [place.area_frac].
